prompt: Swap two int values without using a temporary variable, using only addition and subtraction -- and handle the slot-swapped-with-itself case that breaks the trick.
explanation: Assignment copies a value, so a plain a = b would destroy the old a before it could be saved. Adding the two values first parks the total in one variable, and two subtractions pull each original value back out. Inside an array the same trick has a trap: when i equals j both sides of values[i] + values[j] read the same slot, so it doubles and then cancels itself to 0 -- an early return for i == j is the fix.
hints: Write the three assignments in order: a = a + b, then b = a - b, then a = a - b. Trace them on paper with a = 3 and b = 8.
swapped returns a new array: return new int[] {a, b}; after the swap.
swapInPlace does the same three steps on values[i] and values[j], but guard it first -- if (i == j) return; because swapping a slot with itself has nothing to do.
